## Problem

Since #593 (PR #619), wave>0 PRs open against the real base (`--base main`, `template/src/pdca_harness/publish.py:265` on branch `fix/593-stack-mode-append-only-fold-real-base-prs`) and carry the integration line, which holds **every** earlier-wave bundle of that target, not only the PR's declared prerequisites. So merging any wave>0 PR lands every earlier-wave bundle on the base, including ones the human never approved or has closed.

Reproduced with the real `fold` by the round-3 adversary review: wave 0 = {A, Z}, Z unrelated; B `Depends on` A only. B's PR carries Z's commits. Merge B and Z lands on `main` even if Z's own PR was rejected. Before #593, an own-repo wave>0 PR targeted the line and could not reach `main`.

The round-3 sign-off fixed the docs (a later PR carries those earlier bundles' commits), but the behaviour stays: closing a lower PR does not keep its work off the target. #463 (only declared dependencies need a stacked base) is the nearest issue, but it is about PR bases, not about unapproved content reaching the base.

## Done when

A wave>0 PR cannot land a bundle whose own PR was closed unmerged: either the line carries only the PR's declared prerequisites (#463), or merge/publish refuses while a carried bundle's PR is closed. A real-git test pins the {A, Z} → B case.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_593 iteration-v3 adversary review). Relates to #463.
title: stack mode: merging a wave>0 PR lands every earlier-wave bundle on the base, including ones whose own PR was closed
